sources.name: Wikipedia: Ford Essex V6 engine (Canadian)
sources.says: 3.9: bore 96.8 mm (3.81 in), same as 3.8 and 4.2

sources.name: CarBuzz: The 2004 Ford Mustang only shared this V6 with one other car (G. Smith, 2025)
Ford Performance: 3.9L V6 Essex Mustang (2020, archived)
sources.says: the 3.9 was substantively the same piece as the 3.8 save for a slightly longer stroke

bore_in.note: 96.8 mm = 3.8110 in. Ford implies the 3.8's bore and doesn't print it. CarBuzz's numbers match Wikipedia exactly and may be copied. Treat as borderline.

sources.name: Ford Performance: 3.9L V6 Essex Mustang
sources.says: slightly longer stroke, now at 3.464 inches

stroke_in.note: 88.0 mm = 3.4646 in. Some spec farms say 88.4 mm, which would make it 238 ci.

displacement_ci.note: DISAGREES WITH OUR DATASET (238). cars.com/KBB-style listings say '3.9L/238'. 3.81 x 3.464 x 6 = 237.0 ci.

sources.name: Ford Performance: 3.9L V6 Essex Mustang
sources.says: a 90-degree overhead-valve design built in Ford's Essex Engine Plant

configuration.note: Only Ford Performance gives the 90-degree angle explicitly.

sources.name: Ford Performance: 3.9L V6 Essex Mustang
sources.says: drummed up pallet-loads of 3.9's to finish out the '04 Mustang production run

sources.name: CarBuzz
sources.says: appeared for half a year of 2004 production before becoming exclusive to the Freestar through 2007

sources.name: Wikipedia: Ford Mustang (fourth generation)
sources.says: second half of the 2004 model year, the 3.8 L Essex was replaced with a 3.9 L version

years.note: Both Wikipedia pages count as one source.

sources.name: Ford 2004 Ford Legends brochure (Ford Heritage Vault)
Kelley Blue Book: 2004 Ford Mustang specs

variants.note: Same rating as the 3.8. Ford Performance's 2020 article says Ford didn't change the rating but calls the 3.8 '190', which was the 1999-2000 figure.

unverified.valvetrain: OHV pushrod, 2 valves/cyl: Ford Performance ('OHV, 2-valves-per-cylinder') and Wikipedia. The Ford Legends brochure ('OHV V6') is Ford again. Only 2 independent.
unverified.block_material: Cast iron: Ford Performance (Essex 'compact cast-iron block') and Wikipedia. Only 2.
unverified.head_material: Aluminum: Ford Performance ('aluminum heads') and Wikipedia. Only 2.
unverified.induction: Sequential multiport fuel injection: Wikipedia; Ford Performance says only 'all of them in Mustangs featured fuel injection'. Only 2.
unverified.fuel_type: Gasoline: cars.com Freestar 'Gas V6'. EPA fuel field not checked.

unverified_variants.found: cars.com 2004 Freestar: 193 @ 4500, 240 lb-ft @ 3750 (different peak rpm from the Mustang's 193 @ 5500). Not researched further.
